[Date]

Mrs. Okafor  
Re: Response to October 29 Complaint — Bus 41, Route 9

Dear Mrs. Okafor:

I am writing in response to your complaint dated October 29 regarding Amara’s afternoon bus ride on Tuesday, October 27. My supervisor, Darlene, provided the complaint to me on November 3 and asked me to submit a written statement. I want to explain what I observed, the actions I took, and why I returned Amara to Fairmont Elementary rather than allowing her to leave the bus at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street.

I understand that you were frightened and upset when Amara did not get off the bus as you expected. I have grandchildren, and I can understand how worrying that situation would be. I am sorry for the worry you experienced that afternoon. At the same time, I want to be clear that my decision was made to follow the district’s kindergarten dismissal rule and keep Amara in adult supervision until I could safely release her.

On October 27, I was driving Bus 41 on the Route 9 elementary afternoon run. Amara is a kindergarten student at Fairmont Elementary and has a green tag on her bag indicating that an adult must be present at her stop. The district’s rule for kindergarten riders is that, when no adult is present to receive the student, the child remains on the bus and is returned to school, where the office contacts the parent.

I arrived at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street at 3:52 p.m. The scheduled arrival time was 3:50 p.m. I waited until approximately 3:55 p.m. During that time, I did not see an adult at the corner waiting to receive Amara. Because I could not confirm that an adult was there for her, I kept her on the bus in accordance with the district rule.

I understand from your complaint that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and waved to me. I did not see you or your wave. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street. I cannot say whether it blocked my view of you, but I include that detail because it was part of the conditions at the stop. I was not knowingly ignoring you or refusing to respond. Had I seen you, I would have been able to address Amara’s release according to the district’s requirements.

At 3:56 p.m., I radioed dispatch about the situation. Gloria at dispatch contacted the school. I still had three stops to complete and 14 children remaining on the bus. I continued the route before returning Amara to Fairmont Elementary. I could not leave the children unattended on the bus to walk across the street or search the surrounding area for an adult. My responsibility was to continue supervising the students while following the procedure for a kindergarten child whose receiving adult I could not see.

I arrived back at Fairmont Elementary with Amara at 4:31 p.m. I personally walked her into the school and handed her over to Mrs. Petrakis in the office. I did not leave her outside or send her into the building alone. She remained in my care until I brought her to a school staff member.

During the additional ride, Amara appeared comfortable. She was coloring on her folder and asked whether she could ride more. I told her that we were going on a little extra trip. I share this to describe what I observed while she was with me, not to minimize your concern. I recognize that her experience on the bus and your experience while waiting for her were very different.

I also want to address the statement that I “drove off laughing.” I was not laughing as we left the stop. I was telling a fourth-grade student in seat 2 to sit back down while we were pulling away. That was a direction to a student concerning safe behavior on the bus. It was not a response to you or to Amara’s situation.

For a complete and fair review, I respectfully request that the transportation office promptly preserve and review the available camera footage from Bus 41 for the October 27 afternoon run. In particular, I ask that the review include our arrival and wait at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street, our departure from the stop, and the return to Fairmont Elementary. Please also review any available audio concerning what was said as we pulled away. The recording should be considered alongside this statement and your complaint so that the review is based on the available evidence, not only on our different recollections of the afternoon.

I have been a school bus driver for 28 years without a write-up. I take the safety of the children entrusted to me seriously. I include my work history as part of this formal response, but I also understand that this particular incident needs to be reviewed on its own facts. My reason for keeping Amara on the bus was straightforward: I did not see an adult available to receive her, and the district’s rule required me to return her to school under those circumstances.

Going forward, I would appreciate your help in making sure we can clearly see one another at the stop. Please wait in a safe, visible location on the bus side of the street at the designated pickup point, consistent with the school’s instructions. If you are waiting in a vehicle, please step out when it is safe so I can clearly identify you as the adult there to receive Amara. I am not asking you to enter the roadway or approach a moving bus. If there is uncertainty about where to wait, I would welcome the transportation office’s help in confirming a safe location.

I am glad to continue driving Amara and want her daily ride to remain comfortable and positive. I also want you to feel confident that I will look after her and follow the procedures intended to protect her. I hope this explanation and a review of the camera footage will help resolve the concern and allow us to move forward with a clear understanding of the dismissal process.

Respectfully,

[Driver’s Name]  
Bus 41 — Route 9  
   
cc: Darlene, Supervisor; Transportation Office
